# Signal Landscape Analysis — SIPP Data Lake, Scanner Rules, and Cross-System Signals

## SIPP Data Lake Schema & Capabilities

SIPP brick has sipp_run_query tool (Spark SQL, up to 500 rows). Known databases: adsec (24 tables — peak_score risk scoring, autoprofiler signals), aad (1 table — advanced_actor_results_v2), default (90+ tables — vm_vulnerabilities, vm_metrics, vm_hosts, udd_findings_v2, teams, vpc_flow).

## PEAK Score Risk Factors (27 factors per app)

From adsec.peak_score_gme_latest table. Connectivity factors: aaa_api_count_factor, aaa_indegree_factor, aaa_total_degree_factor, neighbors, shared_vpc. Business criticality: critical_path_factor, resilience, launchpad_tier_1, customer_volume_factor, data_volume_classification. Security risk: classification_factor, shepherd_critical_factor, shepherd_high_factor, custom_idp, kale_processes_factor, kale_stores_factor. Technology: apollo_stage_count_factor, version_set_count, gen_ai_factor, pipeline_external_traffic_factor, pipeline_prod_fabric_factor, customer_device_factor. Composite: unnormalized_peak_score, normalized_peak_score (0-1, likely drives Ring classification).

## Scanner Rules — SAST & DAST Coverage

SAST Rules (139 rules): Hardcoded Credentials (~30+ rules), XXE (8+), XSS (5+), SQL Injection (3+), Command Injection (3+), CSRF (2+), Path Traversal (2+), Deserialization (2+), CORS (2+), JWT (2+), SSRF (2+), plus GraphQL, LDAP, Weak Crypto, Code Injection, File Upload, Open Redirect.

DAST Rules (45 rules): DyePack (~20 rules — XSS 9 sub-types, SSRF, SSTI, XXE, CSRF, Open Redirect, IDOR, Command Injection), Invicti (~15 — SQLi, XSS, File Upload, Web Cache Deception, LFI), Stickler (~10 — JWT, CORS, Security Headers, Cookie Security).

## Shepherd Security Risk Management

Shepherd tracks risks across CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW severity. Campaign types include: Third Party Data Sharing, API Gateway Authentication, IAM User Admin Privileges, Security Group Exposure, Application Security Review Required, Privacy Attestation, Update Operating System, Bedrock EOL Models.

## UDD (User-Defined Detections)

Centralized mechanism for detecting non-compliance across ALL Amazon internal AWS accounts. Owned by AC2 team. Receives CloudTrail events from Nighthawk/Palisade, applies detection rules, produces ASFF findings. Findings flow to Shepherd, Sheepdog, Talos, SIPP. SLA: 99% detection within 30 minutes.

## Cross-Reference Gaps

Artoo has 14 attack agent types. Prompt Injection and AuthZ Bypass have NO scanner rule coverage — novel attack types only AI tools can detect. Inspector findings are 98.9% PACKAGE_VULNERABILITY — completely different signal from SAST/DAST application-level findings.

Signal landscape is fragmented across ~10+ distinct detection systems, each with own data format, severity scale, and remediation workflow.

# Benchmarking & Evaluation Methodology — Research Survey

## Security Tool Benchmarks

Established benchmarks: OWASP Benchmark (2,740 Java test cases, 11 vuln categories), NIST SARD (150+ CWE classes, multi-language), BSIMM16 (122 activities across 111 orgs).

AI Agent Security Benchmarks (Offensive): CVE-Bench (40 real CVEs, CVSS>9, Docker sandboxes — SOTA agents resolve only 13%), TermiBench (510 hosts, 25 services, 30 CVEs, 5 noise tiers — agents can hardly obtain system shells), AutoPenBench (33 tasks in Docker containers), CyberGym (188 open-source projects, 7.5x larger than previous benchmarks), CyberSecEval 2/3 (Meta, 4 test categories), LiveCVEBench (contamination-free, post-training-cutoff CVEs), XOR.tech (128 vulns with verifier + known-good fix).

Ground Truth Generation approaches: Curated Real-World CVEs (scale ceiling: hundreds), Synthetic Generation via multi-agent LLM pipeline (scale: thousands), Commit-Based Mining (scale: tens of thousands), Human-Validated Corpus (scale: low thousands). ART recommendation: hybrid approach combining curated CVEs + synthetic generation.

## Agent Evaluation Frameworks

Five evaluation dimensions: Outcome Correctness (precision/recall), Tool Selection Efficiency, Parameter Construction Accuracy, Resource Efficiency (tokens/time/cost), Trajectory Quality.

Key frameworks: Strands Evals SDK (3 levels — OUTPUT/TRACE/SESSION, 12 built-in evaluators), MCP-Radar (507 tasks, 5 dimensions — significant accuracy-efficiency trade-off), SWE-Effi (token/time/cost effectiveness — discovered 'token snowball' effect and 'expensive failures' pattern), HTC Framework (first formal agentic confidence calibration — overconfidence in failure is fundamental barrier).

## Proposed AutoSec Evaluation Stack (Three Layers)

Layer 1 (Agent Trace Evaluation): Per-run, automatic. Strands Evals OUTPUT/TRACE/SESSION + MCP-Radar 5 dimensions. Integrated into LangSmith/Solera.

Layer 2 (Controlled Benchmarking): Quarterly, reproducible. CVE-Bench methodology + TermiBench noise tiers + CyberGym PoC generation. Ground truth from hybrid approach.

Layer 3 (Production Monitoring): Continuous, real data. Bayesian precision/recall tracking using verified findings as ground truth. Drift detection. Feeds MBR reporting.

Rush wants production metrics (Layer 3), but tools aren't mature enough yet (Artoo 0% precision). Running all three layers in parallel gives the improvement trajectory story.

# Benchmarking Survey — Per-Tool Strategy and Strands Evals Mapping

## Strands Evals Built-in Evaluators

12 evaluators: OUTPUT level (output — requires rubric), TRACE level (helpfulness, faithfulness, coherence, conciseness, harmfulness, response_relevance, tool_selection, tool_parameter), SESSION level (trajectory, interactions, goal_success).

## AutoSec Metrics → Strands Evals Coverage

Direct fit (use today): ToolSelectionAccuracyEvaluator (Artoo agent type selection), ToolParameterAccuracyEvaluator (scan target accuracy), TrajectoryEvaluator (pentest workflow validation), GoalSuccessRateEvaluator (task completion), OutputEvaluator with custom rubrics (finding quality).

Custom evaluators needed: ResourceEfficiencyEvaluator (token/time/cost tracking), CalibrationEvaluator (HTC-based confidence calibration). OutputEvaluator with rubrics can handle SecurityFinding, Coverage, and Pipeline evaluation — only 2 genuinely custom evaluators needed.

## Per-Tool Benchmarking Strategy

Cataphract: Layer 1 — tool selection across 12 vuln sub-classes, token cost. Layer 2 — OWASP Benchmark + CyberGym adapted for Amazon codebases. Layer 3 — Bayesian precision per sub-class from SE-verified findings. Target: 70%+ precision Q4, 95%+ for 4 autonomous sub-classes.

Artoo: Layer 1 — pentest agent type selection (40+ types), OOB callback success. Layer 2 — CVE-Bench for ZF environments + 13 OOB vuln types + TermiBench noise tiers. Layer 3 — Bayesian precision from OOB confirmations. Baseline: 0% precision Dec 2025.

Mycelium: Layer 1 — entity extraction accuracy, RBoM completeness. Layer 2 — compare RBoM against SE-curated app context. Layer 3 — Phase 3 effort reduction from 50-60 hrs baseline.

AutoTriage: Targets — 95% ownership accuracy Q1, 80% reproduction Q2, 80% fix verification Q3.

RAISE AI: CR acceptance rate (54% baseline), remediation time reduction (82% target).

Zero Friction: Setup time 7 hrs baseline → 30 min target.

## Uncovered Gaps

7 gaps nobody owns: pentest engineer effort baseline (NOT MEASURED), issue escape rate (cross-phase), cross-tool precision (no common finding schema), non-web app benchmarks, augmentation quality measurement, longitudinal evaluation, ground truth at Amazon scale (600K apps).
